impact: createServer() calls loadConfig() exactly once (src/server.ts:67) and builds the backend from it, so the running MCP server keeps the config as it was when Claude Code spawned it. Editing .reviewbridge.json (e.g. adding codex_path or changing model) has NO effect on MCP tool calls until the client restarts or reconnects the server — with no indication that the on-disk config is being ignored. This bit a real dogfood session on 2026-07-01: the user fixed codex_path + model in the config, but MCP review_* calls kept using the stale spawn-time values; only the CLI (fresh process per invocation) picked up the fix. Users are TOLD to edit .reviewbridge.json for tuning, so silent staleness is a UX trap during exactly the setup/troubleshooting flows where config changes happen. TRIAGED 2026-07-02 (severity low → medium: bit two dogfood sessions, sits in the install/troubleshoot path): SPLIT into two tickets. (a) Cheap divergence warning — stat the config file at tool-call time; if mtime > server start, emit a one-time stderr note that a restart is needed (~20 lines, no behavior change). (b) Full per-call reload — MUST satisfy the requirements from the 2026-07-02 deliberate-deep plan review: define composite rebuild lifecycle for in-flight reviews, don't rely solely on mtime (1s granularity + same-mtime edits), failure policy for missing/unreadable/validation-fail (not just invalid JSON), treat runtime-reloadable codex_path as a security surface, define effective-config equality, include a test strategy for timing-sensitive paths.
title: MCP server captures .reviewbridge.json at spawn; config edits silently ignored until client restart — consider per-call reload
